mcq.q: Which of the following correctly lists the four stages of the IPOS cycle?
x: Program is not an IPOS stage. A program is the set of instructions run during Process, not a stage of the cycle itself.
Instruction is not an IPOS stage. Instructions are carried out during Process, and Operation is not one of the four stages.
Operating and System are not IPOS stages. The cycle uses Input, Process, Output and Storage, not operating-system terms.
mcq.e: The IPOS cycle is Input, Process, Output, Storage. Input brings data in, Process transforms it, Output presents results, and Storage keeps data and results.

mcq.q: Raw facts and figures are called:
x: Information is data that has been processed and given context, so it is meaningful. Raw facts alone are data, not information.
Knowledge is information applied and understood through experience or learning. Raw figures are not yet knowledge.
Wisdom is the judgment to apply knowledge well over time. Raw facts and figures sit at the lowest level, which is data.
mcq.e: Data is raw facts and figures without context. It becomes information once processed, and it is the base of the data, information, knowledge, wisdom hierarchy.

mcq.q: Software embedded in hardware, such as the BIOS or UEFI, is called:
x: Freeware is software distributed at no cost, not software stored in a device's chips. It is not tied to hardware like BIOS or UEFI.
Middleware is software that connects applications or services, not code permanently stored in hardware.
Shareware is trial software distributed for evaluation with payment expected later. It is not embedded in the device's chips.
mcq.e: Firmware is software stored in a device's non-volatile memory, such as BIOS or UEFI. It initializes hardware and starts the boot process.

mcq.q: Who is called the "Father of the Computer" for designing the Analytical Engine?
x: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline, an early mechanical adding machine in 1642. He did not design the Analytical Engine.
John von Neumann is known for the stored-program architecture. He did not design the Analytical Engine.
Alan Turing is known for the Turing machine and wartime codebreaking. He did not design the Analytical Engine.
mcq.e: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, the first general-purpose mechanical computer design, which is why he is called the Father of the Computer.

mcq.q: Who is considered the world's first programmer?
x: Grace Hopper is a pioneer of compilers and COBOL, not the first programmer. She worked much later than Lovelace's 1843 notes.
Margaret Hamilton led software development for NASA's Apollo guidance work. She is not considered the world's first programmer.
Katherine Johnson was a NASA mathematician who calculated spaceflight trajectories. She is not the first programmer.
mcq.e: Ada Lovelace wrote the first published algorithm for the Analytical Engine in 1843, which is why she is credited as the world's first programmer.

mcq.q: First-generation computers used which core technology?
x: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes in second-generation computers. They came after the first generation.
Integrated circuits were the core of third-generation computers. They came after vacuum tubes.
Microprocessors put a CPU on one chip and defined fourth-generation computers. They are not first-generation technology.
mcq.e: First-generation computers, such as ENIAC and UNIVAC I, used vacuum tubes. They were large, hot, and failure-prone.

mcq.q: Second-generation computers (1956-1963) were built with:
x: Vacuum tubes were the first-generation technology, larger and hotter than transistors. They were replaced in the second generation.
Integrated circuits combine many transistors on one chip and defined the third generation, not the second.
VLSI chips pack huge numbers of transistors on one chip and belong to later generations.
mcq.e: Transistors were smaller, faster, and more reliable than vacuum tubes, which is why they defined the second generation of computers.

mcq.q: "The number of transistors on a chip doubles about every two years" is known as:
x: Amdahl's Law gives the theoretical speedup from parallelizing part of a program. It is not about transistor counts.
Metcalfe's Law says a network's value grows with the square of its users. It is not about chips.
Murphy's Law says anything that can go wrong will. It is a saying, not an observation about chip scaling.
mcq.e: Moore's Law, stated by Gordon Moore and later revised, describes transistor counts on chips doubling roughly every two years.

mcq.q: Who proposed the World Wide Web at CERN?
x: Vint Cerf co-designed TCP/IP and is called a father of the Internet. He did not propose the Web at CERN.
Marc Andreessen created the Mosaic and Netscape browsers. He did not propose the Web at CERN.
Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email and chose the @ sign. He did not propose the Web at CERN.
mcq.e: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989 and built the first web server and browser.

mcq.q: Which computer type is used for weather forecasting and nuclear simulation and measured in FLOPS?
x: Mainframes are large business computers for high-volume transaction processing. They are not the top-end machines measured in FLOPS.
Minicomputers are mid-sized machines for departments or labs. They are not the top-performance class measured in FLOPS.
Microcomputers are personal computers for individual use. They are far too slow for weather or nuclear simulation.
mcq.e: Supercomputers are the fastest machines, used for weather forecasting and nuclear simulation, and their speed is measured in FLOPS.

mcq.q: A speedometer that shows continuously varying values is an example of an:
x: A digital device represents values as discrete numbers, such as a digital clock. A speedometer's continuously varying reading is analog.
A hybrid device combines analog and digital parts. The question describes purely continuous values, so this does not fit.
An embedded device is a computer built into a larger system, such as a microwave controller. It describes where a device sits, not how it represents values.
mcq.e: An analog device represents values as continuously varying quantities, such as a speedometer's needle position, rather than discrete digits.

mcq.q: The ranking of the world's fastest supercomputers is called the:
x: Fortune 500 ranks the largest US companies by revenue. It is not a supercomputer ranking.
Green500 ranks supercomputers by performance per watt, not by raw speed. The question asks about the fastest machines.
Gartner Quadrant is a market analysis chart for technology vendors. It does not rank supercomputers.
mcq.e: The TOP500 list ranks the world's fastest supercomputers, typically by Linpack performance.

mcq.q: Which memory is volatile?
x: ROM is non-volatile and keeps its contents without power. It is not volatile memory.
Flash memory is non-volatile and keeps data without power. It is used for storage, not as volatile working memory.
EEPROM is non-volatile memory that can be electrically erased. It keeps data when power is off.
mcq.e: RAM is volatile, meaning it loses its contents when power is removed, while ROM, flash and EEPROM keep data without power.

mcq.q: MICR is mainly used by banks for:
x: Scanning fingerprints is done by biometric readers. MICR reads magnetic ink characters on cheques, not fingerprints.
Reading barcodes is done by barcode scanners using optical or laser reading. MICR relies on magnetic ink on cheques.
Printing receipts is an output task done by printers. MICR is an input technology for reading cheques.
mcq.e: MICR reads magnetic ink characters printed on cheques, which banks use to process cheque numbers and account details.

mcq.q: How many bits are in a nibble?
x: 2 bits is a single-bit pair, not a nibble. Does not match the correct count of 4 bits.
8 bits is one byte, not a nibble. A nibble is half a byte.
16 bits is two bytes, a word-sized value, not a nibble.
mcq.e: A nibble is 4 bits, half of a byte, and can represent values from 0 to 15 in binary.

mcq.q: The 7-bit character encoding with 128 characters is:
x: Unicode is a large standard covering characters from almost all writing systems. It is not a 7-bit, 128-character encoding.
EBCDIC is an IBM 8-bit encoding used mainly on mainframes. It is not a 7-bit, 128-character set.
BCD is binary-coded decimal, which encodes digits 0 to 9 in four bits. It does not define 128 characters.
mcq.e: ASCII is a 7-bit encoding that defines 128 characters, covering English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes.

mcq.q: Gmail and Office 365 are examples of which cloud service model?
x: IaaS provides virtual machines and raw infrastructure, such as AWS EC2. Gmail is a finished application, not infrastructure.
PaaS provides a platform for developers to build and deploy apps. Gmail is a finished application delivered to users.
DaaS, desktop as a service, delivers virtual desktops. Gmail and Office 365 are delivered as applications, not desktops.
mcq.e: SaaS delivers ready-to-use applications over the cloud, such as Gmail and Office 365, managed by the provider.

mcq.q: Which cloud model provides virtual machines and raw infrastructure (e.g., AWS EC2)?
x: SaaS delivers finished applications such as Gmail. It does not provide raw virtual machines.
PaaS provides a managed platform for building apps, not raw virtual machines. EC2 is raw infrastructure.
FaaS runs individual functions on demand without managing servers. It is not raw virtual machines like EC2.
mcq.e: IaaS provides virtual machines, storage and networks as raw infrastructure that users configure, such as AWS EC2.

mcq.q: Which image format is lossless and supports transparency?
x: JPEG is lossy compression, so it discards detail and does not preserve transparency. It fails both requirements.
GIF is limited to a 256-color palette and only one-bit transparency. PNG supports full alpha transparency, so it is the better fit.
BMP is typically uncompressed and large, and does not commonly support transparency. It does not fit the requirements.
mcq.e: PNG is lossless and supports full alpha transparency, making it the standard lossless image format with transparency.

mcq.q: Which image format is vector-based and scales without loss?
x: PNG is a raster format made of pixels, so it loses quality when enlarged.
BMP is a raster bitmap format made of pixels, not scalable vector paths.
JPEG is a lossy raster format made of pixels, so it does not scale without loss.
mcq.e: SVG stores images as vector paths and text in XML, so it scales to any size without losing quality.

mcq.q: In Excel, which cell reference is an absolute reference?
x: A1 is a relative reference, which changes when the formula is copied to another cell.
A$1:B1 is a mixed range that locks only the row of the first cell, so it is not fully absolute.
#A1 is not a valid cell reference. The hash sign is used for error values such as #REF!.
mcq.e: $A$1 is an absolute reference, with the dollar signs locking both column and row, so it does not change when copied.

mcq.q: The Pascaline, a mechanical adding machine, was built in 1642 by:
x: Gottfried Leibniz built the Stepped Reckoner, which could multiply and divide, in 1672 to 1673. He did not build the 1642 Pascaline.
John Napier invented logarithms and Napier's bones. He did not build the Pascaline.
William Oughtred developed the slide rule. He did not build the Pascaline.
mcq.e: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline in 1642, a mechanical adder that used gears and wheels to add numbers.

mcq.q: Herman Hollerith's tabulating machine for the 1890 US census led to the company later known as:
x: Intel is a microprocessor maker founded in 1968. It did not descend from Hollerith's tabulating business.
Microsoft is a software company founded in 1975. It did not descend from Hollerith's tabulating company.
Apple is a computer maker founded in 1976. It did not descend from Hollerith's tabulating company.
mcq.e: Hollerith's Tabulating Machine Company merged into a group that became IBM in 1924. Hollerith's census machine is the root of IBM.

mcq.q: Which machine is regarded as the first general-purpose electronic digital computer?
x: UNIVAC I was a 1951 commercial computer, later than ENIAC, which was completed in 1945. It was not the first general-purpose electronic computer.
Harvard Mark I was an electromechanical computer built with relays, completed in 1944. It was not electronic.
Colossus was a British electronic code-breaking machine from 1943 to 1944. It was not general-purpose.
mcq.e: ENIAC, completed in 1945, is regarded as the first general-purpose electronic digital computer. It was programmed largely by plugboards and switches.

mcq.q: The stored-program concept (program and data in the same memory) is credited to:
x: Alan Turing described a universal machine in 1936 and worked on early computers. He is not the one credited with the stored-program concept here.
Konrad Zuse built the Z-series machines in Germany. He is not credited with the stored-program concept.
Howard Aiken designed the Harvard Mark I, which used separate instruction and data paths. He is not credited with this concept.
mcq.e: John von Neumann is credited with the stored-program concept, where instructions and data share the same memory, as described in his 1945 EDVAC report.

mcq.q: The first commercially available microprocessor was the:
x: The Intel 8086 came out in 1978, after the 4004 of 1971. It was not the first commercial microprocessor.
The Intel 8080 came out in 1974, after the 4004. It was not the first commercial microprocessor.
The Motorola 68000 came out in 1979, after the 4004. It was not the first commercial microprocessor.
mcq.e: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, is regarded as the first commercially available microprocessor, putting a whole CPU on one chip.

mcq.q: Who introduced the "@" symbol in email addresses (1971)?
x: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN. He did not introduce the @ symbol in email.
Bob Kahn co-designed TCP/IP with Vint Cerf. He is not credited with the @ symbol in email.
Jon Postel was an early Internet standards editor. He is not credited with the @ symbol in email.
mcq.e: Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email in 1971 and chose the @ symbol to separate user name and host name.

mcq.q: Which is the fastest storage location in a computer?
x: L3 cache is a large, slower cache shared by cores on the CPU. Registers are faster and sit closer to the ALU.
RAM is main memory, far slower than registers and cache. It is not the fastest location.
SSD is persistent storage, much slower than RAM. It is not the fastest storage location.
mcq.e: CPU registers sit inside the processor and are the fastest storage location, faster than cache, RAM or SSDs.

mcq.q: Which input technology reads marked bubbles on exam answer sheets?
x: OCR reads printed or handwritten characters and text. It does not detect marked bubble positions on answer sheets.
MICR reads magnetic ink characters on cheques. It is not used for marked bubble sheets.
RFID uses radio tags to identify objects wirelessly. It does not read marked answer sheets.
mcq.e: OMR, optical mark recognition, detects marks in set positions, which is how bubble answer sheets are read.

mcq.q: What is 11111111 in binary equal to in decimal?
x: 256 is 2 to the power 8, the number of values 8 bits can hold, not the largest 8-bit value. Does not match the correct calculation: 11111111 = 255.
127 is the largest 7-bit value, not 8-bit. Does not match the correct calculation.
128 is 10000000 in binary, the 8th bit alone. Does not match the correct calculation.
mcq.e: 11111111 in binary equals 255 in decimal, which is 2^8 minus 1, the largest 8-bit unsigned value.

mcq.q: A translator that converts the entire source code into an executable before running is a:
x: Interpreter translates and executes source code line by line, rather than translating the whole program first. It is not the one that produces an executable up front.
Assembler translates assembly language into machine code. It is a low-level translator, not one for whole high-level programs.
Debugger helps find and fix errors while a program runs. It does not translate source code into an executable.
mcq.e: A compiler translates the whole source program into an executable before running it, unlike an interpreter that translates line by line.

mcq.q: Assembly language belongs to which programming-language generation?
x: 1GL is machine language made of raw binary instructions. Assembly is one level higher.
3GL is high-level procedural languages such as C and Java. Assembly is lower level than these.
4GL is non-procedural languages such as SQL and report generators. Assembly is lower level than these.
mcq.e: Assembly language is a second-generation language, one step above machine code and using mnemonics for instructions.

mcq.q: SQL is classified as which generation of programming language?
x: 3GL languages such as C, Java and COBOL are procedural. SQL is declarative and is classed as 4GL.
2GL is assembly language, which is low-level. SQL is a high-level declarative query language.
5GL is AI and logic languages such as Prolog. SQL is not classed as 5GL.
mcq.e: SQL is a declarative query language, classed as a fourth-generation language because it describes what data is needed.

mcq.q: Which information system supports day-to-day operational-level transactions such as payroll and order processing?
x: MIS gives managers periodic summary reports for middle management. It does not process day-to-day transactions.
DSS helps managers with what-if analysis and decisions. It does not process day-to-day transactions.
EIS gives senior executives summary dashboards for strategy. It is not the operational transaction system.
mcq.e: A Transaction Processing System handles day-to-day operational transactions such as payroll, order processing and inventory updates.

mcq.q: Which system is aimed at senior executives for strategic, long-term decisions?
x: TPS processes day-to-day transactions at the operational level. It is not aimed at senior strategic decisions.
MIS gives middle managers periodic reports. It is aimed at middle management, not senior executives.
Not the answer here: PCS is not the executive information system in this context. The question asks for the system aimed at senior executives.
mcq.e: An Executive Information System or Executive Support System gives senior executives summarized data for long-term strategic decisions.

mcq.q: Which keyboard shortcut opens Task Manager directly in Windows?
x: Not the answer here: Ctrl+Alt+Esc is not the standard Windows shortcut for opening Task Manager.
Alt+F4 closes the active window or app. It does not open Task Manager.
Win+L locks the Windows session. It does not open Task Manager.
mcq.e: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Windows Task Manager directly, without going through the Ctrl+Alt+Del screen.

mcq.q: Colossus (UK, 1943-44) was built mainly for:
mcq.e: Colossus was a British code-breaking machine. Census tabulation is Hollerith's 1890 machine.
x: Census tabulation was the job of Hollerith's 1890 tabulating machine, not Colossus.
Payroll processing is a business data task, not what Colossus was built for.
Weather forecasting is a scientific application, not the purpose of Colossus.

mcq.q: Which information system produces periodic performance reports (sales, inventory, budgeting) for middle managers?
mcq.e: MIS serves middle management with periodic reports. TPS handles operational transactions and DSS provides what-if projections.
x: DSS provides what-if projections for decisions, not periodic reports for middle managers.
TPS handles operational transactions, not periodic performance reports for middle managers.
Not the answer here: EDMS is electronic document management. It does not produce periodic performance reports.

mcq.q: Which raster image format is limited to 256 colors but supports animation?
mcq.e: GIF has a 256-color palette and animation. PNG is lossless with transparency, JPEG is lossy, and BMP is raw.
x: PNG supports full color rather than a 256-color palette, and it is not the animated format asked for.
JPEG is a lossy photo format with millions of colors and no animation. It does not fit the 256-color animated format.
BMP is an uncompressed bitmap format with no animation. It does not fit the 256-color animated format.

mcq.q: Which connector is used for telephone lines?
mcq.e: RJ-11 is the phone connector. RJ-45 is the Ethernet connector.
x: RJ-45 is the Ethernet network connector, not the telephone connector.
PS/2 is a legacy keyboard and mouse connector, not a telephone connector.
eSATA is an external storage connector, not a telephone connector.

mcq.q: The physical parts of a computer that you can touch are collectively called:
mcq.e: Hardware is the tangible physical components of a computer system.
x: Software is the set of programs, not physical parts.
Firmware is software embedded in hardware.
Peopleware refers to the users.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an input device?
mcq.e: A scanner feeds images or documents into the computer.
x: A monitor displays output.
A speaker produces sound output.
A projector displays output.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an output device?
mcq.e: A printer produces a hard copy of information from the computer.
x: A keyboard is an input device.
A mouse is an input device.
A microphone is an input device.

mcq.q: Which of the following is both an input and an output device?
mcq.e: A touchscreen displays output and also accepts touch input.
x: A keyboard only provides input.
A printer only provides output.
A speaker only provides output.

mcq.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
mcq.e: One byte is made up of 8 bits.
x: 4 bits make a nibble.
10 is not the size of a byte.
16 bits is two bytes.

mcq.q: What is the base of the binary number system?
mcq.e: Binary uses only two digits, 0 and 1, so its base is 2.
x: Base 8 is octal.
Base 10 is decimal.
Base 16 is hexadecimal.

mcq.q: Which number system uses the digits 0-9 and the letters A-F?
mcq.e: Hexadecimal has 16 symbols: 0-9 and A-F.
x: Binary uses only 0 and 1.
Octal uses digits 0 to 7.
Decimal uses digits 0 to 9 only.

mcq.q: Which type of memory is non-volatile and commonly stores the BIOS firmware?
mcq.e: ROM keeps its contents without power, so it holds firmware like the BIOS.
x: Cache is volatile.
Registers are volatile.
DRAM is volatile working memory.

mcq.q: An interpreter translates a program by:
mcq.a: Executing the source code line by line
w: Converting all source code into one executable first
Converting source code only into assembly code
Converting machine code back into source code
mcq.e: An interpreter reads and runs source code one statement at a time.
x: That describes a compiler.
An interpreter does not only produce assembly.
An interpreter does not reverse machine code.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an operating system?
mcq.e: Linux is a widely used operating system.
x: Oracle is a database product.
Excel is a spreadsheet application.
Chrome is a web browser.

mcq.q: Which of the following is system software?
mcq.e: A device driver lets the operating system control hardware, so it is system software.
x: A web browser is application software.
A spreadsheet is application software.
A media player is application software.

mcq.q: Which file extension is used by modern Microsoft Word documents?
mcq.e: Word saves documents as .docx files.
x: .xlsx is Excel.
.pptx is PowerPoint.
.accdb is Access.

mcq.q: Every Excel formula must begin with which symbol?
mcq.e: Excel treats a cell entry as a formula when it starts with an equal sign.
x: # is not the formula starter.
@ is not the formula starter.
$ marks an absolute reference.

mcq.q: Which keyboard shortcut undoes the last action in most applications?
mcq.e: Ctrl+Z reverses the most recent action.
x: Ctrl+Y redoes an action.
Ctrl+X cuts.
Ctrl+V pastes.

mcq.q: The Internet is best described as:
w: A private network inside one company
mcq.e: The Internet connects many networks worldwide.
x: It is not one computer.
That describes an intranet.
A browser is just software used to access it.

mcq.q: A private network used only within an organization is called an:
mcq.e: An intranet is a private network for an organization's internal use.
x: The Internet is public and global.
Telnet is a remote login protocol.
Usenet is a public discussion system.

mcq.q: Which cloud service model gives developers a platform for building apps, such as Heroku or Google App Engine?
mcq.e: Platform as a Service provides a ready environment to develop and deploy apps.
x: SaaS delivers finished software.
IaaS provides raw infrastructure.
DaaS is not the model for development platforms.

mcq.q: Which type of memory is faster and is used for CPU cache?
mcq.e: SRAM is faster than DRAM and is used for cache memory.
x: DRAM is slower and used for main memory.
EEPROM is non-volatile and slow.
NAND flash is used for SSD storage.

mcq.q: Which audio format is lossy?
mcq.e: MP3 compresses audio by discarding some data.
x: FLAC is lossless.
WAV is uncompressed.
AIFF is uncompressed.

mcq.q: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations?
mcq.e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit carries out calculations and comparisons.
x: The control unit directs operations.
Cache stores frequently used data.
A register holds data temporarily.
